title: Such stuff as magic is made on: compact operator algebra, stabilizer polytope and the structure of reduced density matrices in a Kitaev spin liquid
authors: Snigdh Sabharwal, Nic Shannon, Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract: Quantum many-body systems exhibit rich and complex behaviour. Magic has recently emerged as a powerful new diagnostic for probing such systems, complementing other key features such as many-body entanglement. Here, starting from an investigation of the onset of magic within subsystems of a larger many-body quantum system, we show that intricate structures emerge which shed important light on the underlying many-body physics. Focusing on the Kitaev honeycomb model, we first identify the temperature below which local subsystems acquire magic. Remarkably, we find that the optimal magic witnesses active at the onset of magic reveal compact operator spaces that continue to capture the local thermal states throughout their subsequent evolution. For the six-site hexagonal marginal, this connection can be made stronger: the same operator space emerges independently from the symmetries of the local marginal and forms the symmetry-resolved plaquette algebra. When these symmetries are realized exactly, the local state lies entirely within this algebra and the reduced robustness of magic is equal to the full robustness of magic. The same reduced description can also be applied to other local quantum resources, which we illustrate using genuine multipartite entanglement. Furthermore, the operator spaces possess a rich algebraic structure in the form of finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras, with a natural interpretation in terms of bond and bond-cycle operators. Our general methodology therefore show how the onset of local magic can reveal a compact, physically meaningful operator structure underlying the finite-temperature Kitaev spin liquid, and opens up a new avenue towards reduced descriptions of quantum resources in many-body systems.
summary: This work introduces 'magic' as a diagnostic tool to probe quantum resources in the Kitaev spin liquid, moving beyond entanglement measures. By analyzing the optimal magic witnesses, the authors show that the local thermal states are constrained to a compact operator space. This space is rigorously characterized as a Euclidean Jordan algebra, offering a powerful, reduced description of the underlying physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the concept of 'magic' (nonstabilizerness) can be used as a diagnostic tool to reveal the underlying compact operator structure governing local quantum resources in many-body systems.
main_result: The optimal magic witnesses reveal that the local thermal states are governed by compact operator spaces that possess the rich algebraic structure of finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebras.
method: The authors use linear programming and optimization techniques to find optimal magic witnesses, which then define an associated operator space whose algebraic structure is analyzed using Majorana fermion representations.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Kitaev honeycomb model (KHM) for spin-1/2, analyzing local reduced density matrices ($ho_A$) for subsystems like the three-site and six-site hexagonal plaquette at finite temperature.
key_observables: Reduced density matrices ($ho_A$), Robustness of Magic ($	ext{RoM}$), Optimal Magic Witnesses ($W$), and the resulting operator space $V$.
important_parameters: Temperature ($ eta$), and the specific geometry of the local marginal (e.g., six-site hexagonal plaquette).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Majorana representation of operators to interpret the algebraic structure of the operator space associated with the stabilizer polytope facets.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate how the magic witness structure reveals a reduced operator space for describing the stabilizer polytope and genuine multipartite entanglement across temperature. Another figure shows the thermal evolution of the $	ext{RoM}$ for various marginal sizes.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by introducing the KHM and the concept of magic, then develops the methodology using $	ext{RoM}$ and optimal witnesses. It applies this to the three-site and six-site marginals, culminating in a detailed algebraic characterization of the resulting operator space.
why_interesting: The development of a general methodology linking quantum resource diagnostics (magic) to specific, structured algebraic frameworks (EJAs) provides a powerful, reduced description for complex, finite-temperature quantum states in strongly correlated models.
